{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Physical examination at every visit is burdensome",
      "quote": "Physical Examination",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Physical examination is scheduled at every visit from screening through EOT, including weekly visits, which is excessive and burdensome for patients and sites.",
      "fix": "Reduce physical examinations to clinically indicated visits only, e.g., at screening, EOT, and as needed for AE assessment."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs at every visit is excessive",
      "quote": "Vital Signsi",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Vital signs are collected at every visit, including weekly dosing visits, which adds time and burden without clear medical necessity for each visit.",
      "fix": "Consider collecting vital signs only at visits where dosing occurs or when clinically indicated, reducing frequency."
    },
    {
      "title": "Adverse event monitoring at every visit including long-term follow-up is impractical",
      "quote": "Adverse Event Monitoring",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "AE monitoring is listed at every visit including EOT and 100DFU, but not at PTFU or LTSFU, which is inconsistent and may miss late AEs.",
      "fix": "Clarify AE monitoring during long-term follow-up; consider collecting only serious AEs and study-related AEs after EOT."
    },
    {
      "title": "Concomitant medication collection at every visit is burdensome",
      "quote": "Concomitant Medication",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Concomitant medication data is collected at every visit, which is redundant and burdensome for patients and sites, especially during long-term follow-up.",
      "fix": "Limit collection to changes in concomitant medications at each visit, or collect only at specified intervals."
    },
    {
      "title": "ECOG performance status not collected at all visits, but physical exam is",
      "quote": "ECOG Performance Status",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "ECOG is collected at fewer visits than physical exam, which is inconsistent since ECOG is a key functional assessment that could be done at every visit.",
      "fix": "Align ECOG collection with physical exam visits or justify the reduced frequency."
    },
    {
      "title": "Screening window of Day -30 to Day -1 is too long for lab assessments",
      "quote": "Screening (Day -30 to Day -1)",
      "page": 22,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "A 30-day screening window is long, and labs collected early may not reflect patient status at baseline, risking eligibility issues and amendments.",
      "fix": "Shorten screening window to 21 or 28 days, and require labs to be repeated if >72 hours before first dose."
    },
    {
      "title": "Physical exam at screening and EOT may be too infrequent for safety monitoring",
      "quote": "A full physical examination will be conducted at Screening and EOT.",
      "page": 73,
      "section": "6.1.8",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The text says full physical exam only at Screening and EOT, but the SoA shows physical exam at every visit, which is contradictory and may confuse sites.",
      "fix": "Clarify in the SoA that full physical exams are only at Screening and EOT, and brief exams at other visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs before cemiplimab infusion may cause delays",
      "quote": "If a study visit occurs where only cemiplimab is administered, vital signs must be collected before the start of cemiplimab infusion.",
      "page": 73,
      "section": "6.1.9",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Requiring vital signs immediately before infusion may cause delays if patients are late; consider allowing vital signs within a window before infusion.",
      "fix": "Specify a window (e.g., within 30 minutes) before infusion for vital signs to reduce scheduling pressure."
    }
  ]
}
